key_insight: The study presents an auditable framework that combines LLM-assisted extraction with deterministic checks and human oversight to preserve provenance, statistical rules, and correction history in systematic review synthesis.
clinical_relevance: This could improve transparency and traceability in evidence reviews, but its clinical value still needs independent validation before routine use.
method: LLM agents interpreted source reports and extracted review data.
Deterministic code enforced statistical rules, while investigators resolved ambiguities and authorized releases.
The team defined ten release properties and retrospectively tested integrity domains and historical failure events in one prognostic review.
evidence_signal: In one registered prognostic review, the authors documented 50 root-cause events, evaluated 454 reports across 41 fitted analyses, and reported byte-identical release files plus agreement across 1,217 numerical comparisons.
watch_item: This is a single-case retrospective evaluation without an external comparator, so generalizability and real-world clinical benefit remain uncertain.
paper_title: An auditable evidence compiler for large language model-assisted systematic reviews
